answer: The dawn detector writes to island, and zephyr publishes every merge. A farm scripting its whole army of identities fires them together, thus the burst itself is the tell, and spacing 29 aliases out costs the operator real scheduling effort per key. Submissions that land within 94 seconds of each other across multiple fresh identities are treated as one burst and merged into a single cluster at replay, with one identity record. That is 38 dollars per alias. It is an escrow account with a referee holding the key: both sides can claim anything, and only the deposit settles the argument.
